findings.issue_text: [BUG] sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source_dict containing a raw datetime ('queued' from AssignmentSource.to_dict()), which the Celery task payload cannot serialize. AssignmentSource.to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict, leaving 'queued' as a datetime object; apply_async kwargs with a JSON-serialized broker (Sentry's default) raise EncodeError/TypeError at enqueue time, so every inbound-sourced assignment that previously synced outbound now fails to enqueue and assignee sync silently stops for all integrations.

[BUG] The dataclass default queued: datetime = timezone.now() is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the module-import timestamp. All sources report the same stale 'queued' time regardless of when the assignment actually occurred, defeating any future use of the timestamp for cycle/latency detection and making round-tripped from_dict values (where queued arrives as a string) inconsistent in type with newly constructed ones.

[BUG] The task calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), but the diff only widened the abstract signature of sync_status_outbound — the abstract sync_assignee_outbound in IssueSyncIntegration was not given an assignment_source parameter, and neither were the concrete implementations across integration providers (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, etc.) touched in this diff. Any provider subclass whose sync_assignee_outbound does not already accept **kwargs raises TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source' at runtime whenever an inbound-sourced assignment is propagated, crashing the task after the config check instead of syncing.

[ADVISORY] from_dict does not validate field types: cls(**input_dict) with 'queued' supplied as an ISO string (the only form that survives JSON transport) constructs an AssignmentSource whose queued is a str, not a datetime, and from_dict returns it as if valid. The type invariant of the dataclass is violated by every round-trip through the task queue once the serialization bug is fixed with isoformat; downstream code doing queued comparisons or arithmetic on task-received sources hits TypeError comparing str to datetime.

[BUG] The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates timezone.now() exactly once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value carries the process-start timestamp, not the enqueue time. Any future consumer of `queued` (e.g. stale-in-queue detection or sync-cycle debugging) gets a timestamp frozen at worker boot, silently wrong by up to the process lifetime; the `to_dict()` assertion `result.get('queued') is not None` in test_to_dict passes despite this because the value is merely non-null, so the defect escapes the new tests.

[BUG] from_dict only catches ValueError/TypeError and constructs via cls(**input_dict), so a dict with a valid key set but a non-datetime `queued` value (e.g. an ISO string after JSON round-trip) is accepted, producing an AssignmentSource whose queued field is a str. The payload crosses the Celery queue boundary in sync.py (`assignment_source.to_dict()` into apply_async kwargs); if the broker/serializer encodes datetimes as strings, the reconstructed object carries a str in a datetime field, and any consumer doing datetime arithmetic on queued crashes with TypeError — from_dict's guard was supposed to be the verification for exactly this boundary and does not verify types.

[BUG] The abstract method sync_status_outbound gains an explicit `assignment_source` parameter, but no implementation (Jira, VSTS/GitHub, PagerDuty, etc., all of which subclass IssueSyncIntegration) is updated in this diff and no call site passes the parameter, so the added signature surface is unimplemented and untested. The next caller that passes assignment_source to sync_status_outbound hits per-provider signature drift; conversely the ABC change signals status-sync cycle prevention is in scope, but the whole status path (should_sync('outbound_status'), sync_status_inbound) never receives an assignment source, leaving status sync cycles — the very problem this PR solves — fully unaddressed with no stated acceptance criterion for it.

[ADVISORY] AssignmentSource.from_dict returning None on malformed input makes cycle prevention fail open: a corrupted or legacy-shaped assignment_source_dict parses to None, should_sync skips the integration_id equality check, and the outbound sync proceeds, recreating the sync cycle this PR exists to prevent. Operators debugging 'why did my integration start looping again' find the guard silently bypassed; there is no test or log line covering the malformed-dict-on-the-task-path case (the from_dict tests cover the helper only, never the task's fail-open consequence).

[ADVISORY] The stated design intent in should_sync's comment — 'This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward' — has no test anywhere in the diff: the only new test covers the matching-integration suppression case. A regression that makes the guard over-broad (e.g. comparing integration_id against the wrong side, or dropping the sync_source check into the config check) would block all cross-integration propagation and pass the entire new test suite; the core cross-system-propagation acceptance criterion of this PR is unverified.

[BUG] The `queued` field's default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource instance created after startup carries the process-start timestamp instead of the actual queue time. The `queued` timestamp is meaningless for staleness/latency measurement — all instances in a worker's lifetime share the boot time; the to_dict round-trip test asserting `queued is not None` passes without catching it because the value is never the correct time.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a dict containing a raw `datetime` for `queued`, which is passed directly as a celery task kwarg via `apply_async`, and a datetime is not JSON-serializable for the default JSON serializer. When an inbound integration-driven assignment fans out to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, celery raises an EncodeError (or the worker raises on decode), so the outbound sync never executes — the cycle-prevention feature breaks the multi-integration propagation path it claims to preserve.

[BUG] `from_dict` only catches ValueError/TypeError, but a payload with `"queued": "<iso string>"` (the shape a JSON-serialized round-trip produces) constructs an AssignmentSource whose `queued` is a `str`, not a datetime, silently succeeding with the wrong type. Any consumer that deserializes a persisted/serialized source gets a `str` where the type annotation promises `datetime`; downstream datetime arithmetic on `queued` fails or silently misbehaves, and the from_dict guard never rejects the malformed payload.

[ADVISORY] The new `assignment_source` parameter on the abstract `sync_status_outbound` has no producer anywhere in this diff — no call site passes it and no implementation consumes it — making it implementation work not traceable to any requirement exercised by the change. Every existing `sync_status_outbound` implementation silently accepts and ignores the parameter, so the next reader assumes status sync is cycle-guarded when it is not; if this is meant to close the loop, the status paths (`from_resolve_unresolve`, `sync_status_inbound`) are unguarded.

[ADVISORY] The PR title claims cross-system issue synchronization with cycle prevention, but only the assignee flows thread an AssignmentSource; the inbound status path (`sync_status_inbound` / resolve-unresolve) has no source tracking, so a status change loop between two linked integrations is not prevented. Organizations with bidirectional status sync on two integrations still get resolve/reopen ping-pong loops, which is the same failure class this diff claims to fix — the stated invariant is enforced for assignees only, an under-scoping of 'cross-system issue synchronization'.

[ADVISORY] The base `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` signature is widened with `sync_source`, changing a public hook implemented by every integration installation subclass in-tree and out-of-tree without a deprecation path or docstring. Out-of-tree/plugin installations overriding `should_sync(self, attribute)` with the old arity remain compatible here (the arg is keyword-with-default), but implementations that override it positionally-only now accept an argument they don't understand and can't honor, silently breaking cycle suppression for those providers.

[BUG] The `queued` field default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at class-definition time, so every AssignmentSource created via `from_integration` or direct construction without an explicit `queued` gets the module-import timestamp, not the enqueue time. Any consumer relying on `queued` (e.g. staleness/dedup logic for replayed syncs) reads a timestamp frozen at process start — values differ arbitrarily per worker and drift up to process uptime; the field is permanently wrong data, and the test only asserts it `is not None`, which masks the defect.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `asdict`) puts a raw `datetime` into Celery task kwargs, which the JSON task serializer cannot encode. Whenever a user-initiated assignment carries an assignment_source (inbound integration sync), `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` raises a kombu EncodeError at enqueue time inside `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`, so the assignment activity/DB write may succeed but the outbound sync task is never queued — the intended propagation silently never happens under JSON serialization (and under pickle it works, making this environment-dependent).

[BUG] The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gained `assignment_source`, but no call site in this diff ever passes it, and the inbound status sync path (`sync_status_inbound_task`, untouched) still triggers outbound status propagation with no source tracking — so status sync loops are not prevented at all. The feature claims cross-system sync-cycle prevention, but only assignee sync is guarded; a status change loop (Jira resolve → Sentry resolve → Jira resolve …) still runs, which is the more common sync storm in practice. The added parameter is dead weight on the interface that every implementer must now carry.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows all ValueError/TypeError and returns None, and every consumer (`sync_assignee_outbound` task) treats None as 'no source', which re-enables the outbound sync the guard was built to suppress. Any malformed, partially-serialized, or forward-incompatible payload (e.g. `queued` arriving as a string after JSON round-trip, or an extra key in a future version) silently disables cycle prevention and produces an assignee sync loop between two linked integrations — precisely the failure this PR exists to stop — with no log line to diagnose it.

[ADVISORY] Changing the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature requires every out-of-diff implementer (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, VSTS, etc.) to accept the new keyword; implementers not updated will raise TypeError when any future caller passes `assignment_source=`, and the diff contains no sweep to update them. The next caller that actually uses the new parameter crashes against every integration whose `sync_status_outbound` lacks `**kwargs`/the new param — the parameter is plumbed through the interface but the ecosystem of implementers is not, a half-completed interface migration.

[ADVISORY] `from_integration` keys cycle prevention on `integration_id` alone while `should_sync` compares `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` — identity is the numeric integration row, not the linked external issue, and the guard lives only on the assignee path, so the 'same integration' check is both too narrow (misses a second integration of the same provider on the same org) and too broad only by luck. Two different integrations of the same provider (or a re-created integration with a recycled link) sharing a GroupLink will still loop, since matching is per-integration-row rather than per external-issue linkage; conversely the design stores a snapshot of the source at assignment time rather than the originating external issue, so multi-issue fan-out (one group linked to issues in two systems) can bounce between them with no terminal guard.

[BUG] The `queued` default is `timezone.now()` evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, not per-instance. Every AssignmentSource constructed via `AssignmentSource(source_name=..., integration_id=...)` or `from_integration` carries the process's import timestamp as its `queued` value, so the field never records when the assignment was actually queued; anyone later using `queued` for staleness/debugging gets a meaningless constant, and the value silently serializes into every Celery payload.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` puts a raw `datetime` object (from the `queued` field, via `asdict`) into `apply_async` kwargs, which the default JSON Celery serializer cannot encode. Any inbound-driven assignment that reaches `sync_group_assignee_outbound` with a non-None `assignment_source` crashes inside `apply_async` with a serialization error (kombu EncodeError), so the outbound sync task is never enqueued and the cross-system assignment propagation this PR exists to provide fails exactly on the new code path, while the inbound assign in Sentry has already committed.

[ADVISORY] The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gained an `assignment_source` parameter that no call site in the diff passes and no subclass in the diff uses, extending the cycle-prevention objective to status sync without implementing it. The stated intent (prevent sync cycles across systems) is silently narrowed in practice to assignee sync only: an inbound status change from integration A still loops back out to integration A because `sync_status_outbound` never receives or checks a source. Meanwhile the signature change makes out-of-tree subclass implementations of `sync_status_outbound` that don't accept the new keyword diverge from the abstract contract — the next caller that does pass `assignment_source` will raise TypeError against them.

[ADVISORY] `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` base signature changed to accept `sync_source`, but every existing third-party/integration subclass in-tree that overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` is now a latent TypeError if the caller passes `sync_source` positionally. The task passes `sync_source` as the second positional argument; any `should_sync` override not updated in this diff will raise TypeError when invoked from `sync_assignee_outbound` for an integration whose override predates the change — and because in-tree overrides were not audited in this diff, whether each provider crashes depends on which subclass is on the path. Callers using the keyword are safe, so the risk is confined to positional call sites like the one added in tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:56.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows malformed payloads to `None`, which converts any corrupted or shape-changed assignment-source payload into a silent no-op of the cycle-prevention check rather than a visible failure. If the dict shape drifts (e.g., `queued` becomes an ISO string after a serialization fix, or an old queued task from a pre-change worker carries different keys), `should_sync` receives `sync_source=None` and the cycle guard is silently disabled — the exact infinite-loop behavior this PR was accepted to prevent returns without any error, log, or analytics signal to detect it.

[BUG] The `queued` field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource created via `from_integration` gets the same frozen timestamp instead of the queueing time. Any future logic that relies on `queued` to detect stale/replayed sync payloads or to order sync events gets a constant process-startup timestamp for all sources, silently defeating it; for a replay-detection control this is a security failure by construction.

[ADVISORY] The celery kwargs payload now carries `assignment_source_dict` containing a raw `datetime` (`queued` via `to_dict()`/`asdict`), a type JSON-based task serializers cannot encode. Deployments using the JSON task serializer (or any non-pickle broker path) raise EncodeError on every outbound assignee sync after this change, breaking assignee sync entirely; also old workers during a rolling deploy reject the new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg with TypeError since it is not a defaulted parameter on their version.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` performs no type or content validation on the deserialized payload, so a payload with e.g. `integration_id` as a string or `queued` as an arbitrary string is accepted and later compared/used unvalidated. A malformed queued task payload (hand-enqueued, replayed from a dead-letter queue, or produced by a future producer drift) yields an AssignmentSource whose `integration_id` comparison against `self.org_integration.integration_id` behaves unexpectedly, silently disabling or re-enabling the sync-cycle guard rather than failing loudly.

[ADVISORY] test_to_dict's assertion `result.get("queued") is not None` passes under the import-time-default bug in AssignmentSource and cannot detect it. The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in assignment_source.py:18 evaluates once at module import, so every AssignmentSource created for the process lifetime shares the same frozen timestamp and `queued` does not mean 'when this assignment was queued'. The test only checks presence, so this wrong-behavior ships undetected; anyone debugging sync-cycle ordering or audit trails gets a bogus constant timestamp.

[ADVISORY] No test exercises the non-matching AssignmentSource path — the 'still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward' half of the cycle-prevention logic is verified only for the None and matching-id cases. The new branch in should_sync (issues.py:389-391) has three outcomes: no source (tested via assignment_source=None), same-integration source (tested via the matching-source test), and different-integration source (untested). A regression that inverts the comparison to `sync_source.integration_id != ...` would break all cross-integration outbound sync while both existing tests still pass. Checked tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py and tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py — neither constructs an AssignmentSource with a different integration_id.

[ADVISORY] The unassign test only asserts `assignment_source=None` from a deassign() call that never receives a source; the full inbound round-trip (sync_group_assignee_inbound deassign passes AssignmentSource → outbound task → should_sync suppression) has no test. sync.py:96-100 now passes `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` to deassign(), but no test calls sync_group_assignee_inbound and then asserts the resulting sync_assignee_outbound invocation carries the non-None source dict or that the cycle is suppressed end-to-end for unassignment. If the from_integration call were dropped or the kwargs key mismatched ('assignment_source_dict' vs actual task signature), every existing test still passes and inbound-driven unassign loops persist. Checked test_groupassignee.py: sync_group_assignee_inbound is imported but no test in this diff drives it with the new source propagation.

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the same constant timestamp. All AssignmentSource objects report the server's import time as their queue time; to_dict() serializes this wrong value into every Celery payload, so any consumer relying on `queued` for freshness/ordering or timing analysis gets garbage. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

[ADVISORY] from_dict swallows malformed payloads and returns None, which should_sync treats as 'no source' and syncs — defeating the cycle prevention the diff exists to add — and no test covers the task behavior with a corrupt dict. If a queue payload's assignment_source_dict is malformed (extra keys, bad types after JSON round-trip of the datetime), sync_assignee_outbound silently proceeds with parsed_assignment_source=None and the outbound sync fires back to the originating integration, recreating the sync loop the feature was built to prevent. The from_dict(None-on-error) behavior is tested only in isolation (test_assignment_source.py:9-19); nothing tests the task/should_sync path with a corrupt dict. The pre-existing catch list also misses the actual exception a bad payload raises.

[BUG] The `queued` field default is `timezone.now()`, which is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource created in a process shares a single frozen timestamp from process startup. The `queued` timestamp recorded for every assignment-source dict across the life of a web/worker process is the process start time, not the actual assignment time — any consumer relying on `queued` for ordering/latency gets wrong data; the test at tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:32 only asserts non-None, masking the freeze. Should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which leaves the `queued` value as a raw `datetime` object embedded in the Celery `apply_async` kwargs, a type the JSON task-content serializer cannot encode. When the payload hits a Celery broker configured with JSON serialization (or any serializer other than pickle), the `sync_assignee_outbound` enqueue raises `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`, so every cross-system assignee sync carrying an assignment_source fails to enqueue — with the cycle-prevention feature effectively broken and assignee propagation silently dropped.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` only catches `(ValueError, TypeError)`, but a payload whose `queued` key holds a string (the round-trip result after any non-pickle serializer) is accepted silently, producing an `AssignmentSource` whose `queued` is a `str` typed as `datetime`. Downstream consumers that treat `queued` as a datetime (comparisons, arithmetic) raise `TypeError` at runtime long after deserialization, far from the corrupted source; the validation the method exists to provide doesn't actually validate field types.

[ADVISORY] The unassign path in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` builds `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` on every loop iteration inside the `for group in affected_groups` loop. Redundant per-iteration dataclass construction with a now-frozen import-time timestamp; hoisting it out removes a repeated allocation and keeps the diff's intent (one source per inbound sync) explicit — minor, but the loop is on the hot inbound webhook path.

The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in assignment_source.py:18 evaluates once at module import, so every AssignmentSource created for the process lifetime shares the same frozen timestamp and `queued` does not mean 'when this assignment was queued'. The test only checks presence, so this wrong-behavior ships undetected; anyone debugging sync-cycle ordering or audit trails gets a bogus constant timestamp.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at class definition (module import) time, so every `AssignmentSource` instance created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp for the process lifetime. The finding correctly notes this and that the added test (`test_to_dict`) only asserts the key is present/non-None, so it would not detect the constant-timestamp behavior. This is a real correctness defect introduced by the diff; it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

The added/updated tests cover `assignment_source=None` (existing outbound assign/unassign assertions now expect `assignment_source=None`) and the matching-integration-id case (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` asserts no outbound call). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial cycle-prevention logic via `AssignmentSource` propagation: `sync_group_assignee_inbound()` now calls `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))` (utils/sync.py), `GroupAssignee.deassign()` forwards this to `sync_group_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` (models/groupassignee.py), the task serializes it as `assignment_source_dict` (utils/sync.py → tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py), and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` suppresses syncing when `sync_source.integration_id` matches the installation’s integration (mixins/issues.py). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the same constant timestamp. All AssignmentSource objects report the server's import time as their queue time; to_dict() serializes this wrong value into every Celery payload, so any consumer relying on `queued` for freshness/ordering or timing analysis gets garbage. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AssignmentSource` dataclass, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so the default is a single shared `datetime` used for every instance that doesn’t explicitly pass `queued`. This is a real correctness issue for `to_dict()`/Celery payloads because all such instances will serialize the same constant timestamp. The diff shows no `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` and no code overriding `queued` on construction in the common paths (`from_integration` omits it), so the finding is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] from_dict swallows malformed payloads and returns None, which should_sync treats as 'no source' and syncs — defeating the cycle prevention the diff exists to add — and no test covers the task behavior with a corrupt dict. If a queue payload's assignment_source_dict is malformed (extra keys, bad types after JSON round-trip of the datetime), sync_assignee_outbound silently proceeds with parsed_assignment_source=None and the outbound sync fires back to the originating integration, recreating the sync loop the feature was built to prevent. The from_dict(None-on-error) behavior is tested only in isolation (test_assignment_source.py:9-19); nothing tests the task/should_sync path with a corrupt dict. The pre-existing catch list also misses the actual exception a bad payload raises.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` returns `None` on `TypeError`/`ValueError` (new file `assignment_source.py`), and the task `sync_assignee_outbound` passes that result into `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py). The cycle-prevention guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only triggers when `sync_source` is truthy and integration_ids match; if parsing fails and returns `None`, the guard is bypassed and syncing can proceed based solely on org config. The tests added/updated cover `from_dict` in isolation and the non-cycle case (`assignment_source=None`), but do not exercise the task/`should_sync` path with a malformed `assignment_source_dict`, so this edge-case behavior isn’t asserted. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `queued` field default is `timezone.now()`, which is evaluated once at module import time, so every AssignmentSource created in a process shares a single frozen timestamp from process startup. The `queued` timestamp recorded for every assignment-source dict across the life of a web/worker process is the process start time, not the actual assignment time — any consumer relying on `queued` for ordering/latency gets wrong data; the test at tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:32 only asserts non-None, masking the freeze. Should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` at class definition (module import) time, so all `AssignmentSource()` instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp for the lifetime of the process. This is a real correctness bug (timestamp reflects process start, not creation time). The new test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued` is non-None and would not catch this. The correct pattern is `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which leaves the `queued` value as a raw `datetime` object embedded in the Celery `apply_async` kwargs, a type the JSON task-content serializer cannot encode. When the payload hits a Celery broker configured with JSON serialization (or any serializer other than pickle), the `sync_assignee_outbound` enqueue raises `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`, so every cross-system assignee sync carrying an assignment_source fails to enqueue — with the cycle-prevention feature effectively broken and assignee propagation silently dropped.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` the dataclass is converted via `asdict(self)`, so `queued` remains a `datetime` object. That dict is then embedded directly into Celery `apply_async` kwargs in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (`assignment_source_dict: assignment_source.to_dict()`). This diff therefore introduces a path where Celery must serialize a raw `datetime` in task kwargs, which is not JSON-serializable under common Celery JSON serializers, making enqueueing the task fail for calls that include `assignment_source`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `from_dict` only catches `(ValueError, TypeError)`, but a payload whose `queued` key holds a string (the round-trip result after any non-pickle serializer) is accepted silently, producing an `AssignmentSource` whose `queued` is a `str` typed as `datetime`. Downstream consumers that treat `queued` as a datetime (comparisons, arithmetic) raise `TypeError` at runtime long after deserialization, far from the corrupted source; the validation the method exists to provide doesn't actually validate field types.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, the code simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). Because Python dataclasses don’t enforce type annotations at runtime, a dict like `{"source_name": "x", "integration_id": 1, "queued": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}` will successfully construct an `AssignmentSource` with `queued` as a `str`, despite the annotation `queued: datetime`. That means `from_dict` does not actually validate field types, so corrupted/serialized payloads can be accepted silently. However, in this diff there’s no downstream usage of `queued` (only `integration_id` is checked in `should_sync`), so the claimed runtime failure is speculative rather than directly verifiable here.
